purpose: PINN and DeepONet pricers for eight-stock arithmetic basket options, each built as a ladder: every level adds one technique to the configuration below it, and every level is scored on the same validation contracts. Level names and techniques are those of the four-stock ladders, so the two studies compare level by level.
selection_rule: Within each family the level with the lowest validation score is selected. Score = mean over price and the 82 Greeks of RMSE / RMS(reference) on the 4,096 validation contracts drawn from the protocol's training domain. A level within 1% of the best score yields to the earlier level.

computational_domain.note: Spatial extent of the PDE problem in z = log basket forward moneyness and the forward shares s_i >= share_floor (the simplex), like a grid solver's far boundary. The training domain maps into z in [-0.52, 0.46] and shares of at least about 0.016 (weight floor 0.04 times the smallest forward ratio). sigma, the factor-model correlation matrices and the maturity cap are the protocol's training domain; tau starts at 0 because the PDE starts at the payoff.

reference_rule.note: Rules of the torch reference (src/neural/reference.py): one scrambled Sobol net over the seven residual factors with the geometric control, seeded by seeds.reference_rule (labels) and seeds.reference_rule + 1 (evaluation), so the monitor and validation references do not share the labels' rule error. Tensor Gauss-Hermite, the four-stock choice, needs 32^7 points. Phase 0 (experiments/reference/rule_check.py) measures each rule's error on the development contracts; check it before training and raise the points if the evaluation rule's error is not well below the networks' errors.
